title: WKT Validator: Syntax and Structure Checks
description: Validate Well-Known Text geometry with the WKT Validator — keyword, parentheses, coordinate and ring-closure checks in one pass. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, POLYGON ((0 0, 10 0, 10 10, 0 10)) fails ring closure — first pair (0 0) never repeats at the end — and the validator names that exact fault instead of a generic 'invalid'.
quick_answer: The WKT Validator checks a Well-Known Text geometry for syntactic and structural validity — correct keywords, balanced parentheses, numeric coordinate pairs, closed polygon rings and sane nesting. Paste the WKT and read a specific verdict: valid, or the particular fault and where it sits.

body.t: A CSV of WKT headed for PostGIS gets sampled and validated first; one bad row found here saves a rolled-back import at midnight.
Your generator emits WKT that the database rejects. The validator's named fault (unbalanced parens at a position, a stray third ordinate) localises the generator's bug.

Self-intersecting rings pass syntax yet fail geometry rules; the validator separates 'parses' from 'sound' so you know which class of trouble you hold.

examples.label: Example · The comma family of errors

body.t: POINT (-73.9855, 40.758) is wrong in WKT — coordinates inside a pair are space-separated, commas separate pairs. Half the invalid WKT on Earth is that one comma, imported from GeoJSON habits and everyday writing.
A bow-tie POLYGON (edges crossing) is perfectly formed WKT and broken geometry. Two verdicts, both reported: syntax valid, ring self-intersects. Conflating them is how bad data gets a clean bill.

popular_table.note: Validity has layers — lexical, syntactic, geometric (OGC simple-features rules). The validator reports which layer failed; all three passing is the real 'valid'.

faq: Ring self-intersection (the bow-tie class) is screened and reported as a geometric fault, distinct from syntax errors. Full OGC validity suites in a database remain the deepest audit.
EWKT's SRID=4326; prefix is accepted and the SRID reported; the geometry after it is validated normally.
POINT Z, LINESTRING M, ZM forms validate with their declared dimensionality applied consistently across all tuples.
POINT EMPTY and kin are valid WKT — validated as proper empties, not errors.
Recognised as types; their control-point structure is checked lexically, while true arc-geometry rules sit beyond this validator's stated scope.
It says valid but PostGIS rejects it.

PostGIS adds its own strictness (and geography-type casting rules). The usual suspect is ring orientation or a type/SRID mismatch — the validator's layer report tells you syntax is innocent, pointing the hunt at semantics.
One string per pass here — the gatekeeper for samples and suspects; column-scale validation belongs in the database's own ST_IsValid pass, specified by this same rule list.
